d: A weathered crest depicting the mark of Lordaeron. With so few relics left after the kingdom's fall, someone in the Undercity would be very keen to get their hands on this.
p: What have you got there, adventurer? A tasty morsel?
c:
Well I'll be. A genuine relic of our home. Mostly intact, too. We need to be extra careful with this one.
Thank you for your aid in restoring our history, adventurer. I'll see to it that we take good care of this.

d:
We're getting ready to send a team of rams to reinforce the Alterac expedition, but we've run out of material to make their saddles.
Collect pelts from the largest, fiercest leopards to the east and bring them to me. It's biting cold up there and our forces deserve nothing but the finest pelts to keep them warm!
p: You look chilly, adventurer. How goes the hunt?
c: These pelts will make excellent saddles. You've done the Alliance proud, adventurer!

d:
The keg is stamped:
BLASTING POWDER - DANGER - DO NOT HANDLE - DANGER - QUARRYMASTER AUTHORIZATION ONLY - DANGER
You get a sinking feeling that the troggs shouldn't have this. It would be best to report this to the quarry sooner rather than later.
This keg held enough powder to turn King Magni's throne room into an open air courtyard. We've got to get it back from the troggs before they work out how to ignite it.
p: I hope you've got good news for me?
c:
That should be all the stolen powder. Thank you, adventurer.
Please accept this reward, and... I'd appreciate if you didn't mention this little incident to anyone.

d:
Welcome to the most vital organ of the Undercity: The Apothecarium! Here we experiment on the most virulent of Azeroth's exotic specimens.
You've caught me in a good mood, so I will let you in on my latest investigation. It appears there is a particularly venomous arthropod stalking the ruins above our fair city. Its toxins are said to eat through even undead flesh. How exhilarating!
I wish to validate these claims. Should you find yourself withering away from its bite, I should love a sample.
p:
Any fool can tell you the most potent transmission method will always be through the blood.
I must see this strain for myself!
c:
You killed it??
Hmmph. Lucky for you this should be enough ichor to reverse engineer its properties. I would have expected more from a fellow alchemist.
Get out of my sight!

d:
So you're looking to learn the blacksmith's trade? Maybe we can help each other.
The supply shipment's late, and I need materials for some repairs around the camp. If you get me what I need, I'll teach you some of my techniques. Sound fair?
p: Don't slack off, friend. Smithin' isn't for the lazy!
c:
You're a resourceful one, friend.
Now listen up - I'm not going to repeat myself!

d:
Ah, a fellow traveler. It's about time Lordaeron sent reinforcements.
My master has already charged into the fray and has ordered me to maintain my post. It has been quite some time, however.
I don't dare trust this task to any of these filthy half breeds, but if I could impose on you a favor, I beg of you to find me the Grand Marshal. He is the tallest, most statuesque hero you've ever laid eyes on. You'll know him when you see him.
p: Good to see you're still alive and kicking! How fares the battle? Have you seen my lord?
c:
Truman looks at the head of his former lord in horror and disgust.
Is this... Some kind of joke? Why would you bring me this monstrosity's head?
Get out of my sight! I should have known better than to trust someone who allies themselves with the type of filth you do. The true sons of Lordaeron will reclaim our home. And when we do we'll finally be free to purge it of beasts and those who consort with them like you!
